messages:
Asha (PM): Heads up — planning a short 'coda' sprint to clear a backlog of catalog onboarding items and nail down deprecation windows. Need to align on scope and customer-facing commitments.
Miguel (Eng): 👍 what are the must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
Asha (PM): Must: 1) smoke evals for new models (latency + basic quality checks), 2) pin prioritization rules, 3) deprecation notice SLAs and migrations playbook.
Elaine (ML): For smoke evals we should require: perf baseline (p95 latency), safety quickchecks, and 3 golden prompts pass rate >= 85%. Anything looser risks regressions.
Sam (ProdOps): From ops POV: we need clear rollout gates — canary on 5% of traffic, 24h health window, auto-fallback to previous model. Also a doc describing rollback triggers.
Miguel (Eng): Agree. Can we codify pin prioritization as: customer tier + traffic % + recent errors? I can prototype a scoring function: score = 0.5*tier + 0.3*traffic_norm + 0.2*(1-error_rate).
Asha (PM): Prototype sounds good. Need to map tiers to numeric values (free=0, pro=0.7, enterprise=1). Also decide whether marketing customers get exceptions.
Elaine (ML): One wrinkle: some models degrade quietly on LLM metrics — detection needs small evaluation set per customer. That increases eval cost. We should define a threshold for when we run per-customer smoke evals (e.g., monthly if >1% traffic).
Raj (SRE): Ops constraints: deprecation windows should default to 60 days for non-enterprise, 90 days for enterprise, with option to extend for contract terms. Deprecating model also needs capacity fallback plan so traffic doesn't spike other pools.
Asha (PM): Drafting a short SLA doc. Proposal: public notice 30 days before deprecation announcement, then 60/90 day customer migration window. Wait — public notice before announcement seems weird. We'll say announcement -> 60/90 day migration window + weekly migration status reports for affected customers.
Sam (ProdOps): Also include a migration kit: compatibility shim config, recommended replacements with mapping table, and a sample code snippet for SDK callers. Example snippet: `client.generate({ model: 'redwood-open-7b-v2', fallback: 'redwood-open-7b-v1' })`
Miguel (Eng): On the rollout side, we need an automated canary job that validates correctness against golden prompts and checks that token cost delta < 15%. I can add that to CI.
Elaine (ML): For acceptance we should tie to evals in Optimize: regression alert if metric drop > 5% on golden set OR hallucination score increases by X. We'll define X after one run.
Asha (PM): OK action items: Miguel — prototype scoring function and canary job (owner). Elaine — define smoke eval checklist and threshold numbers. Sam/Raj — draft migration kit + ops runbook. I'll draft the customer comm timeline and SLA language.
Miguel (Eng): I can have the first prototype by EOW. Quick question: should pin exceptions be a manual approval by product or auto by score threshold?
Asha (PM): Let's do hybrid: auto-keep for score > 0.85, manual review for 0.6-0.85, auto-deprecate if <0.6 but notify owner. We'll iterate.
Raj (SRE): FYI, onboarding more per-customer evals increases KV cache pressure during canaries — ops needs quotas. Add that to the runbook.
Sam (ProdOps): Noted. Will add quota recommendations and a small billing note for eval runs (to avoid surprises).
onboard-bot: Reminder queued: 'catalog-coda-sprint' planning sync tomorrow 10:00. Attachments: sprint checklist stub.
Asha (PM): Great. If no major objections I'll lock the sprint scope midday tomorrow. Please drop any edge cases in this thread before then. :sparkles:
Miguel (Eng): One edge: legacy clients using v1 API with pinned weights — need a conversion path. I'll draft a migration snippet.
Elaine (ML): Also include guidance for quantized variants; some customers pinned to FP16 will see changes. Add to migration mapping.
Asha (PM): Thanks — adding both to the backlog. Closing for now, will post the formal scope doc in the channel after I consolidate.
